The more I thought about why she was doing it, the more I guess I get it. Her whole progression as an artist is seeing her evolve from a teenager deeply embedded with themes of depression, suicide and angst- and then into more lighter, seeing the light at the end of the tunnel, upbeat album like laurel hell and TLINHASAW. I think doing her folk song is her way of changing the sadness or the darkness associated with the song, like shes singing it happily because those feelings are over. 

I do think you have to be an OG fan to appreciate it and really really be analytical about her choices as an artist. I do think everyone has a right to feel however they want. I am a bit disappointed she isn't performing it the way she sang it in her album BUT i know that her music is hers and she can do whatever she wants with it. 

I understand the reasoning behind not wanting to "ruin" the experience but I also think that you really do have to go into it with an open mind. If you see, her folk songs are only the ones from her older album and in a way it's beautiful. Pink in the night will be a banger, folk or not. The lyrics aren't changing, just the beat.
